assigned.title: An LGPL-compatible libmpv and FFmpeg the product may actually ship
assigned.acceptance: The libmpv and FFmpeg binaries the installer ships are built under terms this product may distribute, and the evidence is recorded rather than assumed. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 9 names two traps and RESEARCH_PLAYBACK.md already found the equivalent defect elsewhere -- 'every prebuilt ffprobe on npm is a GPL-3.0 binary, and several declare otherwise' -- so a downloaded build is not evidence of its own licence. REQUIRED: the configure flags that keep the build LGPL are stated and reproducible, and any GPL-only component is named and excluded. REQUIRED: the written-offer and attribution obligations LGPL imposes on a shipped binary are satisfied by something in the installer, not by a sentence in a README nobody ships. REQUIRED: the exact upstream versions are pinned and recorded, because PW-0207's error mapping is built against a specific header. NOT IN SCOPE: any decoder whose distribution needs a patent licence this project does not hold -- if one is required, stop and report it as a commander decision rather than shipping it.
assigned.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. SURFACE NOTE: this task's allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet. The evidence-based narrowing procedure applies to reconciling work already in history; for genuinely new work the surface is the smallest set of paths the acceptance can be satisfied within, and it is narrowed again from the diff before review if it turns out to be wider than what was written.

build.evidence:
npm run build (turbo): 12 tasks successful, 0 failures. STATED PLAINLY AGAIN, as the previous recording of this gate did: apps/desktop is not an npm workspace, so none of this round's changes are build inputs and most of those tasks are cache hits. A build gate on a change the build graph cannot see is close to vacuous, and the evidence that matters is below.

WHAT THIS ROUND ADDRESSED, AND WHICH OF gpt-architect's NINE BULLETS IT IS. The round-111 verdict's last bullet: "strict notice generation fails on missing evidence rather than silently producing a green result". IT DID NOT, AND THAT IS NOW FIXED AND PROVEN.

THE DEFECT, EXACTLY. `collect-notices.mjs` walks `<sidecar>/server/node_modules`. If that directory was missing, empty, or laid out somewhere the walk does not read, `collect()` returned zero entries, `renderNotices` produced a document listing nothing, the script wrote it, printed "0 package(s), 0 with no licence evidence" and EXITED 0. `--strict` could not catch it: it fires on `attention.length > 0`, and a tree with no packages has nothing to attend to. So the strictest available setting was GREEN on the one input where the evidence was entirely absent -- an installer built on it would have shipped a confident, empty attribution claim.

That is the third instance of one shape in this project: `drizzle-kit migrate` applying nothing and exiting 0 (PL-0714, and again when PL-0726 found the hand-written replacement had grown its own version), and three e2e titles skipped in every configuration with no gate asking (PL-0717). Each reported success over an empty set.

THE FIX, IN TWO PLACES ON PURPOSE. `collect-notices.mjs` refuses a tree it found no packages in, and reads its own output back to confirm a non-empty file exists. `package-sidecar.mjs` then asserts the file is in the tree it is about to hand the bundler -- the same fact from the other side, because one asks "did I write it" and the other asks "is it in what ships", and a step inserted between them that cleaned the directory would leave the first passing.

PROVEN AGAINST REAL TREES, not described. Five cases, driving the actual script as a child process:
  A. a real-layout tree with two packages          -> exit 0, "2 package(s), 1 with no licence evidence", 1618-byte document
  B. --strict on it, one package lacking evidence  -> exit 1, the original behaviour, unchanged
  C. server/ present, node_modules absent          -> exit 1, "found no packages", AND NO DOCUMENT WRITTEN
  D. server/node_modules present and empty         -> exit 1
  E. --strict on the empty tree                    -> exit 1. This is the regression that mattered: it was 0 before.

AND THE TESTS WERE PROVEN NON-VACUOUS BY REMOVING THE FIX. With the empty-tree refusal deleted from collect-notices.mjs, `node --test apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs` goes 22 tests / 19 pass / 3 FAIL, naming exactly the three new refusals. Restored, 22/22, and `git diff --stat` confirms the file is the fixed one. A control case is in the suite too -- a tree that HAS packages still being described -- because a script that refused everything would satisfy every refusal assertion.

WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVEN, AND IS NOT CLAIMED. Eight of the verdict's nine bullets are about THE CONTENTS OF A REAL WINDOWS PACKAGE TREE, and no such tree exists to inspect: Windows #14's `package` job failed, and Windows #15's (run 37210126408) was still IN PROGRESS when this was recorded. Specifically unproven: whether a libmpv/FFmpeg artifact is included at all and its provenance, version pin and configure flags; whether GPL-only components are excluded; whether THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md is actually present in the installed tree; whether the Node LICENSE is beside the shipped runtime; and whether the collected dependency list reflects what was really packaged. The mechanism for every one of those exists and is now harder to fool, which is not the same as having looked.

TWO MECHANISM GAPS FOUND WHILE LOOKING, NEITHER FIXABLE FROM THIS SURFACE (apps/desktop/** and docs/LICENSING.md):
  - `scripts/windows/verify-install.mjs` requires four paths of the INSTALLED tree and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md is not among them. The one check that inspects a real installation does not ask for the file the attribution obligation depends on.
  - `apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs` -- now 22 cases, including these five -- is still run by nothing automatically. apps/desktop is not a workspace and `npm run test:scripts` is in the root package.json. The same gap PL-0714 closed for two other suites.
Both are filed rather than reached into.

THE PATENT BOUNDARY IS UNTOUCHED, as the verdict requires: nothing here enables, assumes or infers anything about H.264/HEVC, and no decoder was added, configured or claimed.

review.evidence:
CHANGES REQUESTED at 659cafa118bdc72b98d43c7f3fa21a120222e57b. TRANSCRIBED BY claude-lead from gpt-architect's round-111 verdict document, which lists PW-0208 under "NOT APPROVED YET" and says: "PW-0208 still requires stronger evidence about the contents of the actual Windows package/distribution tree."

The same document's section 3 states what that evidence has to cover, and it is quoted here in full rather than paraphrased, because it is the acceptance this task is now being measured against:

  - actual libmpv/FFmpeg artifact included, if included
  - exact provenance/version/pin
  - build/configuration evidence available for what ships
  - GPL components excluded where required by the selected LGPL distribution strategy
  - THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES or equivalent actually present in the package tree
  - Node licence actually present beside the shipped runtime where required
  - dependency licence collection reflects the actual packaged dependencies
  - written-offer/attribution material actually appears where the distribution strategy requires it
  - strict notice generation fails on missing evidence rather than silently producing a green result

AND THE BOUNDARY IT RESTATES, which this task's own acceptance already carries: "Do NOT guess the H.264/HEVC patent decision. H.264/HEVC remains a commander/legal decision and must remain explicitly separate from the LGPL evidence. Do not enable patent-dependent functionality based on an assumption."

WHAT THE VERDICT IS OBJECTING TO, read plainly: the distinction between evidence about SOURCE AND SCRIPTS and evidence about THE TREE THAT SHIPS. The recorded `build` gate is about what the packaging is configured to do. "The actual Windows package/distribution tree" is what came out of it, and the round-110 instruction said the same thing in fewer words -- "Do not infer packaged contents solely from source intent."

Returned to IN_PROGRESS. The gate results are discarded by `request-changes` as the control plane intends: the `build` gate described a tree, and the next one has to describe the tree that is actually inspected.

assigned.title: Corrective: the Windows negative-verification step fails whether the check passes or not
assigned.acceptance:
WINDOWS #16 (run 37215304869, head 1474d0b) FAILED AT `verifier-negative`, and PW-0602's step-id diagnostics named it: "FIRST FAILING STEP: verifier-negative (failure). Everything after it did not run." Trail: everything before it success, lifecycle=skipped, upload-installers=skipped.

THE STEP CANNOT SUCCEED. It is:

  $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
  node scripts/windows/verify-install.mjs "${env:TEMP}"
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { throw "..." }

Refusing is this step's SUCCESS case, so `node` exits 1 when everything is right. PowerShell 7.4 stabilised `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference`, which makes a native non-zero exit a TERMINATING error under `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"`. Where it is on, line 2 throws before line 3 runs. The step fails if the verifier refuses (PowerShell throws) and fails if it accepts (the explicit throw fires).

REPRODUCED: the container's pwsh 7.4.6 defaults the preference to False and the step exits 0 -- which is why no local check caught it. Forcing it true gives exactly the runner's failure: 'Program "node" ended with non-zero exit code: 1.'

REQUIRED: the step succeeds when the verifier REFUSES a non-install, and fails when it ACCEPTS one. Both directions, and the second is the one that matters -- this step exists because a verify-install.mjs that returned 0 unconditionally would make every lifecycle PASS meaningless.

REQUIRED: the behaviour does not depend on the runner's default for that preference. A step whose correctness turns on an image's PowerShell configuration is a step that will break again when the image moves, and this project cannot observe that from here.

REQUIRED: the step REPORTS THE EXIT CODE IT SAW, as an annotation. Annotations are the only CI channel this session can read, and the cause above is inferred from a reproduction rather than from the runner's log -- the next run must be able to confirm or refute it without a login.

REQUIRED: no other step is touched, and nothing about what verify-install.mjs checks changes. This is a shell-semantics defect in one step.

FORBIDDEN: deleting the negative check, or softening it to a warning. It is what keeps every positive lifecycle result honest, and its own comment says so.

NOT IN SCOPE: why the lifecycle harness has never run. That is a consequence of this, and whether anything ELSE then fails is the next run's evidence.
assigned.notes:
FILED ROUND 112 by claude-lead from Windows #16's job page. Classification C (workflow/harness defect) under the round-112 scheme: not a product defect, not a defect in verify-install.mjs, and not caused by PL-0729 -- the verifier exited non-zero against a non-install both before and after that task, correctly.

P0 because it blocks the entire Windows packaging and lifecycle path: lifecycle=skipped and upload-installers=skipped on every run that reaches it, so F1/F2/F3/F4 have never executed and no installer artifact has ever been published.

.github/workflows/windows.yml is reserved by no ACTIVE task (PW-0501, PW-0602, PW-0107 all DONE).

unit.evidence:
THE STEP WAS EXTRACTED FROM THE WORKFLOW AND DRIVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS UNDER BOTH PREFERENCE SETTINGS, so what was executed is the text CI will execute. Extracted with yaml.safe_load from jobs.package.steps[id=verifier].run, with only ${env:TEMP} parameterised so a second directory could be substituted.

THE DEFECT, REPRODUCED FIRST. The ORIGINAL step, against a non-install directory, with $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference forced true:

  Program "node" ended with non-zero exit code: 1.
  exit 1

That is the runner's failure, reproduced in this container. The `node` line threw before `$LASTEXITCODE` was read, so the step failed WHEN THE VERIFIER DID THE RIGHT THING. With the preference false -- this container's default -- the same original step exits 0, which is why no local check ever caught it and why it survived two rounds.

THE REPAIRED STEP, FOUR RUNS:

  preference inherited TRUE   non-install dir  -> step exit 0, annotation "verify-install exited 1", "correctly refused"
  preference inherited TRUE   complete install -> step exit 1, annotation "verify-install exited 0", threw "passed against a directory that is not an install"
  preference inherited FALSE  non-install dir  -> step exit 0, annotation "verify-install exited 1", "correctly refused"
  preference inherited FALSE  complete install -> step exit 1, annotation "verify-install exited 0", threw

IDENTICAL UNDER BOTH, which is the requirement: the step's correctness no longer depends on the runner image's PowerShell configuration, which this repository cannot observe from outside and which is what moved under it.

AND THE CHECK IS NOT WEAKENED -- THE SECOND ROW IS THE PROOF. The acceptance says the direction that matters is that the step FAILS when the verifier ACCEPTS a non-install, because a verify-install.mjs returning 0 unconditionally would make every lifecycle PASS meaningless. Driven against a COMPLETE synthetic install -- the one input where the verifier legitimately returns 0 -- the step throws, exactly as before. Nothing was deleted and nothing became a warning.

THE EXIT CODE IS NOW ANNOUNCED, as the acceptance required, because the diagnosis above came from a reproduction rather than from the runner's log and annotations are the only CI channel this session can read. The next Windows run states the code out loud whichever way it goes, so it confirms or refutes the diagnosis without a login.

NOTHING ELSE MOVED. `git diff` over .github/workflows/windows.yml is confined to this one step. The workflow parses: yaml.safe_load reports jobs package and e2e-desktop. All eight pwsh blocks were parse-checked with [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile -- the new step parses clean, and the only two that do not are the step-trail block and the annotation publisher, both of which contain ${{ }} Actions expressions that PowerShell cannot parse and GitHub substitutes before the shell sees them; with those substituted, both parse.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE. That the lifecycle harness then succeeds. It has never run -- `lifecycle=skipped` on every observed Windows run -- so whether F1/F2/F3/F4 pass is the NEXT run's evidence and is deliberately not claimed here. What this task removes is the step that made reaching them impossible.

recommended.title: Updates, and a version the application can prove
recommended.acceptance: The application can tell a user what version it is and can update itself safely, or states plainly that it cannot yet and why. REQUIRED: an update mechanism whose payloads are signature-verified -- an updater that fetches and executes an unverified binary is a remote code execution feature, and SECURITY.md's threat list already ranks unauthorized access above convenience. REQUIRED: the update endpoint is pinned and allowlisted like every other egress in this repository. REQUIRED: a rollback story, or a stated decision that there is none and what a user does instead. REQUIRED: the version is derived from one source shared with PW-0501. IF SIGNING IS UNAVAILABLE the update path must be disabled by default and say so, rather than shipping an unverified one -- an unsigned auto-updater is worse than no updater, and that dependency goes to LAST_MILE rather than being worked around.

recommended.title: A CI step that hangs reports 'in progress' for six hours instead of failing
recommended.acceptance:
REQUIRED: the jobs in ci.yml and windows.yml get `timeout-minutes`, per step where a step has a credible hang and per job otherwise. THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE. PL-0735 fixes the one step that hangs today; this makes the NEXT one visible. A step with no bound burns GitHub's six-hour default and reports 'in progress' the entire time -- indistinguishable, to the only readable channel this project has (annotations, because job logs need a login), from a runner that is merely queued. That is how CI #181 and #182 both sat unfinished without anyone treating it as a failure.

REQUIRED: each bound is derived from an OBSERVED duration and the derivation is written beside it. A number somebody felt was generous is a number somebody will raise the first time it fires. Observed today: e2e 5m 8s, e2e-typecheck 12s, and the Windows e2e-desktop job 3m 25s.

REQUIRED: the bound is not so tight that a slow runner reads as a defect. A timeout that fires on a cold cache teaches people to re-run rather than to read, which costs more than the hang.

OUT OF SCOPE: the control-plane performance work, which is PL-0735, and any change to what the steps do.
recommended.notes:
SPLIT OUT OF PL-0735 in round 112, carrying its clause verbatim. PL-0735 was filed holding ci.yml and `ai:claim` refused it on an overlap with PL-0728, which is in REVIEW for the rest of the round. Keeping both halves in one task meant neither landed; this one is BACKLOG until ci.yml frees.

Classification C (workflow/harness defect) under the round-112 directive's A-E scheme, same as PL-0735. P1 rather than P0 because PL-0735 removes the hang that exists; this prevents the one that does not exist yet.

recommended.title: The logs directory the shell creates is written to by nothing, and the sidecar's stderr is discarded
recommended.acceptance:
FOUND WHILE WRITING PW-0603's RUN SHEET, not by looking for it. The certification document's defect-report format asked the commander for "the log file (location established by PW-0501)". There is no such file, and there is no code that could write one.

MEASURED IN THE SHELL'S OWN SOURCE, three facts that together close the question:
1. `windows_host.rs` calls `std::fs::create_dir_all` on data, cache and logs at first launch, and passes the logs path to the sidecar as LIBERTY_SIDECAR_LOG_DIR. The directory is real.
2. NOTHING EVER WRITES INTO IT. A grep of apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/ for File::create, write_all, fs::write and OpenOptions returns nothing; every `write!` in the crate is a Display impl formatting an error string. The crate declares no `log` or `tracing` dependency and tauri.conf.json configures no plugins, so there is no logger to have been wired.
3. THE SIDECAR'S OUTPUT IS DISCARDED. `command.stderr(Stdio::null())` -- a Node stack trace printed on the way down goes to the kernel's bit bucket. stdout is piped to a reader thread whose lines are consumed only by `await_handshake`; once the handshake resolves or the launch is abandoned the thread keeps draining the pipe and throwing each line away, by design, so the child never blocks.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT LOST, because this is a diagnosability defect and inflating it would be the same error in the other direction. `failure.rs` already gives the viewer seven NAMED failure headlines covering the anticipated paths -- missing installation, unwritable profile, loopback not secured, unsafe start, service did not finish starting, service reported something unusable, service keeps stopping -- and the commander screenshots those. What is lost is the UNANTICIPATED failure: the sidecar starts, throws, prints the only explanation that exists to stderr, and exits, and the shell can say no more than "the local service did not finish starting". That is the whole of the evidence for a launch defect on a packaged build, on a machine no engineer can reach.

REQUIRED: the sidecar's stderr is captured rather than discarded, and its stdout keeps being drained for the same reason it is drained today. A pipe that is read and then written to a file is still read; this must not reintroduce the full-pipe deadlock `windows_host.rs` already explains.

REQUIRED: what is captured lands in the directory the shell ALREADY creates and already names to the sidecar -- %LOCALAPPDATA%\app.projectliberty.desktop\logs. Do not invent a second location, and do not make the layout depend on %LOCALAPPDATA% being read in a second place: sidecar.rs owns the SHAPE under a root the host supplies, and that division is deliberate.

REQUIRED: bounded. An unbounded log on a long session is row E1's failure wearing a different hat. State the bound -- size, count or both -- and make it a tested property rather than a comment.

REQUIRED: the handshake token NEVER reaches the file. `token.rs` mints the one secret this process owns, PW-0101 exists to keep it from another process on the same machine, and a log file in a world-readable profile directory that echoed a line containing it would hand it over. Prove this with a test, not with care.

REQUIRED: a test that the file is actually written, driven through the same path a launch takes, and a test that a sidecar which exits noisily leaves its output behind. `sidecar-bootstrap/acceptance.mjs` already drives a real child and already sets LIBERTY_SIDECAR_LOG_DIR; that is the honest place to assert from, off Windows.

REQUIRED: docs/WINDOWS_CERTIFICATION.md's "There is no application log file" subsection is rewritten to say where the log is, in the same edit. A stale subsection claiming the absence of a file that now exists is the exact failure this repository recorded in round 112 for diagnostics-disclosure.tsx.
recommended.notes:
FILED BY claude-test DURING PW-0603, round 112, classification A (product defect) under the round-112 directive's A-E scheme. It is a real defect in the shipped desktop shell, not a packaging or harness fault and not a CI condition.

WHY P2 AND NOT P1, stated so gpt-architect can overrule it cheaply. The product works without this; what suffers is the evidence a failure leaves behind. Most rows the commander can run TODAY are install-path rows, and those already produce an msiexec /l*v log plus verify-install.mjs's own named refusal. The undiagnosable case is narrower: an unanticipated sidecar failure during launch (matrix rows A1, A2, A3b). That is squarely inside the round-112 directive's priority 1 -- desktop launch and runtime qualification -- which is the argument for P1, and the reason this reasoning is written down rather than left as a number. If the first RIG launch defect comes back with only a screenshot, that settles it.

NOT DONE SPECULATIVELY. PW-0603 ships the sheet with the absence stated plainly and the report format limited to what actually exists, so the commander is never asked for a file that was never written. The sheet names this task, so closing this task has a documentation obligation attached to it, which is the REQUIRED clause above.
